name: Plague of Amwas
summary: Outbreak of bubonic plague at the Syrian garrison town of Amwas (Latin Emmaus) in 638-639, during the Arab consolidation of the Levant following the Yarmuk campaign. Several thousand of the Muslim army perished, including senior commanders Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah and Shurahbil ibn Hasana. The early Islamic discussion of the proper response, whether to flee the affected area, generated foundational hadith-jurisprudential material on contagion and divine decree.

_quarry.structural_significance: Stripped the first generation of Companion-commanders from the army of Syria in the immediate post-conquest decade. Hodgson treats it as one of the contingent shocks that shaped the institutional improvisation of the Rashidun caliphate.
